title: Engagement-linked pricing heuristic drafts
content:
Goal: sketch a compact set of heuristics that tie customer pricing to engagement (rather than raw tokens), so we:
- reward low-latency interactive use cases (many short calls)
- avoid punishing long background-batch embedding jobs unfairly
- keep meter simple enough for marketing + self-serve signup

Quick context / why this:
- Current token-based units are clean but noisy for chat/product-UX customers: a 30s chat session and a 1-hour batch embed job can consume similar tokens but are different revenue/expectation patterns.
- We want a middle path: preserve per-token transparency for power users while offering a session/engagement abstraction for most apps.

Assumptions (back-of-envelope values — replace with infra numbers):
- baseline hosted model cost (amortized compute + infra + egress): $0.0004 / 1k tokens (conservative low-end)
- average message size (user prompt + model response): 200 tokens
- average messages per interactive session: 6 (so ~1.2k tokens / session)
- marginal storage / KV cache amortization per active session: $0.0001
- churn: 30% 7-day retention for free tier users (used for activation credit sizing)

Heuristic ideas (sketches):
1) Session credits with token floor and overflow pricing
   - Each session consumes a session-credit bucket. A session-credit buys up to X tokens (default X = 1.5k).
   - If session uses <= X tokens, charge 1 credit. If > X tokens, bill 1 credit + per-token overage at standard token rate.
   - Credits are sold in bundles (e.g., 100 credits = $Y). For UI: show credits as "interactive sessions".
   - Rationale: simplifies pricing for chat UX, aligns with typical session token distribution.
   - Quick math: if X=1.5k tokens and cost per 1k tokens is $0.0004, break-even per credit should be ~0.0004*1.5 = $0.0006 (plus margin/ops).

2) Engagement bands (short / medium / long)
   - Classify session by message count or duration: short (<3 messages), medium (3-12), long (>12).
   - Charge: short=0.5 credit, medium=1 credit, long=1 + overage per 1k tokens.
   - Pros: granular, can be gamed but easy mental model for customers.

3) Activation credits & decay (for free tier onboarding)
   - Give 10 activation credits on signup valid for 14 days. Credits consumed per session as above.
   - Credits decay (or reduce allocation) if account dormant for >30 days. Helps prevent credit-mongers.

4) Hybrid: per-call minimal fee + token rate for big jobs
   - Small per-call fixed charge (e.g., $0.00005) to capture request overhead (routing, cold-start risk).
   - Token rate still applies for >Y tokens per request.
   - Use for API-first customers who do many tiny calls (micro-interactions).

5) Committed tier conversion (for Dedicated / enterprise customers)
   - Map credits to committed throughput units. E.g., 1 Dedicated CU = 50k session-credits / month (discounted).
   - Allow overage at lower per-token penalty and automatic fallbacks to hosted models to avoid hard failures.

Unit-econ worked example (starter numbers):
- Starter app: 10k DAU, 2 sessions/day/user => 20k sessions/day => 600k sessions/month.
- If average session = 1.2k tokens => tokens/month = 720M tokens.
- Infra cost (0.0004 / 1k) => cost = 0.0004 * 720k = $288 / month. (note: convert token units carefully; 720M tokens / 1k = 720k)
- If we price session-credit = $0.02 / session (starter retail) => revenue = 0.02 * 600k = $12k/month. Margin looks healthy; we can tune.

Sanity checks & pitfalls:
- Overage complexity: Too many micro-rules will confuse billing and support. Keep the default simple: 1 credit = ~1.5k tokens and a visible per-token overflow rate.
- Gaming: apps can split or batch calls to optimize credits. Consider thresholds / detection heuristics and anti-abuse (e.g., X calls within Y seconds from same session collapse).
- Transparency: Users must see exact token equivalence in Console + per-route breakdown. Important for trust.

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Launch internal experiment with 3 cohorts (pure token, session-credit default, hybrid). Small sample of new signups for 6 weeks.
- Metrics to track: ARPU, churn at 14/30/90d, support tickets about billing, average tokens/session, fraction of traffic hitting overflow.
- Instrument Console: show "credits spent" + token-equivalent and projected monthly cost in USD.

Open questions / things to get numbers for:
- Real infra amortized cost per 1k tokens by model family (redwood-1-small, redwood-2-medium, open-embed-1).
- Distribution of session lengths (message count) across top 200 customers.
- Typical embed jobs vs interactive ratio by customer segment.
- Sensitivity: how much does ARPU change if credit size X = 1k vs 2k tokens?

TODOs (next steps):
- Ask infra team for per-model per-1k-token cost matrix (ticket to PRIC-412).
- Build a quick Simulator (spreadsheet) to run scenarios for DAU/MAU mixes and per-route model choices.
- Draft copy for Console UX explaining credits -> tokens mapping (simple explainer + link to "show raw tokens").

Notes to self: keep this world simple at launch. Users should always be able to switch back to raw tokens if they prefer exact accounting. We can productize credits later as "interactive packs" with auto-renew and committed discounts.

References/links (quick):
- convo-length-dist analysis: GH:analytics/usage/session-lengths.csv
- prior brainstorming: shared_drives/product/packaging/session-based-pricing-rough.md

Rough headline tier examples (marketing-friendly):
- Free: 50 session-credits / month, 10-day activation credits, community support
- Starter: 1k credits / month ($20) + standard token overflow at $0.00045 / 1k tokens
- Growth: 10k credits / month ($150) + 10% discount on overflow
- Enterprise: Custom committed credits + private deployments + SLA

End of scratch notes.
